title: Console feature de-escalation, acceptance gates, and rollback playbook for dashboards/tracing/cost
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Context: As part of the Console rebaseline effort we need a disciplined, deliverable-focused de-escalation of non-essential surface area for the dashboards/tracing/cost breakdown feature set so we can ship a reliable 2025.04 release. This ticket captures the product decisions to reduce scope, the acceptance gates that must be met before enabling advanced tiles, and a concrete rollback/playbook in case telemetry or performance regressions occur post-rollout. Rationale: recent perf stress tests and early beta feedback show that the full planned surface causes backend QPS spikes and increases per-route p95 by more than the budgeted 40ms for some enterprise tenants. Rather than delay the release, we will: 1) cut non-blocking exploratory tiles and advanced filters from the initial deploy, 2) implement gated rollout flags for tracing sampling and cost-heavy breakdowns, and 3) define automatic rollback criteria tied to observability SLOs and revenue-impacting signals.
acceptance_criteria: Core dashboard tiles (Route Latency, Token Cost, Request Rate) render within SLO: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 250ms under baseline load
Tracing: basic span listing and trace viewer must support up to 2,000 concurrent open trace sessions across dedicated clusters without OOMs
Cost breakdown: route-level aggregated cost shows daily rollups and per-token aggregation (approximate) for last 7 days; exact per-token attribution deferred
Advanced gates disabled by default: sampling-control UI, per-customer heavy-cost drilldowns, and anomaly-auto-alerts are behind feature flags
Feature flags and rollout config exposed in Console -> Admin and documented in runbook
End-to-end smoke tests (UI + API + ingestion) pass in staging and can be executed by CI in < 15 minutes
Have documented rollback playbook and automated alerting rules created in PagerDuty/Datadog channels
Stakeholder approval: PM, Eng lead (runtime), Design lead sign-off in comments
decisions: Remove 'explorer tile set' (free-form filtering & user-saved views) from initial launch to reduce backend indexing load
Expose sampling and heavy cost breakdowns behind admin-only flags; default OFF for new tenants
Defer per-token exact attribution to runtime-1.19 when KV cache metrics and quantized accounting are available
Adopt a 2-week canary window with staged percentage ramp for tenants with >1k daily requests

rollout_strategy: Stage 0: Disabled by default for all tenants; internal smoke for 24 hours
Stage 1 (Canary): Enable for 3 internal tenants and 5 small customers (1%) with manual monitoring for 48 hours
Stage 2: Ramp to 10% of eligible customers over 7 days if SLOs hold
Stage 3: Global enable for eligibile tenants; advanced features remain admin-only until runtime-1.19
rollback_playbook: Trigger: any of the following fires: sustained p95 latency > 2x baseline for 30m, error rate increase > 0.5% absolute, memory OOM on tracer-worker or cost ingestion backlog > 12h
Step 1: Flip 'console_2025_cost_tracing_safe_mode' feature flag to OFF (global) via admin API
Step 2: Notify on-call runtime lead and PM via PagerDuty; post incident channel with initial assessment
Step 3: If global flip not possible, disable specific routes/add temporary rate-limits on heavy endpoints
Step 4: Run lightweight cleanup job to flush ingestion backlog and clear slow queries
Step 5: After stabilization, run reduced-scope validation plan and only re-enable under canary with 48h monitoring
notes: This ticket intentionally reduces UX richness in favor of reliability and predictable economics for the release.
Engineering will produce a post-mortem template for any rollback event tied to this rollout with cost delta calculation.
Once runtime-1.19 provides improved KV accounting and sampling hooks, we will re-evaluate reintroduction of advanced tiles.
